registered: 2026-11-25, before KinematiK's rotor model was run on this test. DISCLOSURE: the measured maxima (87 and 79.6 C) and the paper's own analytical maxima (88.5 and 81.5 C) were read before this file was written; the inputs were taken from the paper's Tables 1-4 without adjustment.

source.reference: Yevtushenko, Kuciej, Grzes, Wasilewski: Analytical Model of the Frictional Heating in a Railway Brake Disc at Single Braking with Experimental Verification, Materials 15(19), 6821, 2022 (open access, CC BY)
source.test: Full-scale railway brake dynamometer, UIC 541-3 thermocouples 1 mm below the friction surface; the hottest one at r_eq + 40 mm = 0.293 m

inputs.disc: cast iron, OD 0.64 m, ID 0.35 m, thickness 0.055 m, k 51 W/mK, rho 7100, c 500

mapping: KinematiK's OneDRotor (finite slab, half thickness 27.5 mm, both faces heated, explicit finite differences) driven by the paper's own frictional heat flux into the disc at r = 0.293 m, q_d = eta gamma f p(t) V(t) r / Rw, with the pressure ramp and velocity of its eqs. (12)-(17); no convection or radiation during the stop (as in the paper's model), temperature read 1 mm below the surface.
